'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Attacks on civilians in the Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***A [[Russian Armed Forces|Russian]] missile strike on [[Sloviansk]], [[Donetsk Oblast]], kills at least eight [[civilian]]s and injures 21 others. [https://www.nytimes.com/2023/04/14/world/ukraine-strike-sloviansk-toddler.html (''The New York Times'')]
*[[Yemeni civil war (2014–present)|Yemeni civil war]]
**A major [[prisoner swap]] of nearly 900 prisoners begins between rival factions in [[Yemen]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20230414-major-yemen-prisoner-swap-under-way-as-first-plane-leaves-icrc (AFP via France 24)]
*[[Mali War]]
**The [[Islamic State in the Greater Sahara]] encircles the strategic town of [[Ménaka]] in [[Ménaka Region]], [[Mali]]. [https://www.theafricareport.com/300081/mali-sahel-based-jihadists-threaten-key-town-of-menaka-gao-region/ (''The Africa Report'')]
*[[Ituri conflict]]
**At least 42 people are killed by suspected [[CODECO]] militants during a raid at a village in [[Ituri Province]], [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]]. [https://apnews.com/article/eastern-congo-militia-civilians-killed-05f2efb7636ec163a3c49987eda8ef1a (Associated Press)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2023 Tunisia migrant boat disasters]]
**The death toll from a [[list of migrant vessel incidents on the Mediterranean Sea|boat that sank off the coast]] of [[Tunisia]] increases to 33 after eight more bodies are found. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/tunisian-coastguard-finds-more-bodies-migrant-shipwreck-toll-rises-33-2023-04-14/ (Reuters)]
*One person is killed and 70 others are injured after a bridge collapses in [[Udhampur District]], [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu and Kashmir]], [[India]]. [https://apnews.com/article/bridge-collapse-kashmir-india-2f65ffa266b8756a0c844d09f5e9ab2e (AP)]
*At least four people are killed and thirteen others are injured after a fire breaks out in a shelter in [[Recife]], [[Pernambuco]], [[Brazil]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/fire-childrens-shelter-brazil-leaves-least-4-dead-13-injured-2023-04-14/ (Reuters)]
'''Health and environment'''
*[[Ghana]] becomes the first country to approve [[University of Oxford|Oxford]]'s [[malaria vaccine]] R21/Matrix-M. [https://www.pharmaceutical-technology.com/news/ghana-becomes-first-country-to-approve-oxfords-malaria-vaccine/ (Pharmaceutical Technology)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[LGBT rights in Tanzania]], [[Capital punishment in Tanzania]]
**[[Tanzania]]n members of [[National Assembly (Tanzania)|parliament]] call on the [[Government of Tanzania|government]] to tighten laws against [[homosexual]] sex with the [[death penalty]]. [https://www.thecitizen.co.tz/tanzania/news/national/mps-call-for-tough-laws-on-same-sex-relations--4196442 (''The Citizen'')]
*[[Cannabis in Quebec]]
**The [[Supreme Court of Canada]] upholds [[Quebec]]'s [[Provinces and territories of Canada|provincial]] ban on homegrown [[cannabis]] despite a 2018 federal ruling which allowed small quantities of cannabis to be grown at home. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/canadas-top-court-upholds-quebecs-ban-homegrown-cannabis-2023-04-14/ (Reuters)]
*Twelve people are killed after riots break out in a prison in [[Guayaquil]], [[Guayas Province|Guayas]], [[Ecuador]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/gang-clash-leaves-least-12-dead-ecuador-prison-2023-04-15/ (Reuters)]
'''Science and technology'''
*The [[United Kingdom]]'s [[Department for Transport]] approves [[Ford Motor Company]]'s [[Self-driving car|hands-free driving vehicles]] on 2,300 miles (3,700 km) of motorways in [[England]], [[Scotland]] and [[Wales]]. The UK [[History of self-driving cars|becomes the first]] European country to approve hands-free driving technology on public roads. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/business-65272929 (BBC News)]
*[[Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer]] (JUICE) is launched by the [[European Space Agency]] (ESA) to search for life in the [[Moons of Jupiter|Jovian system]], with an expected arrival date of 2031. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/science-environment-65258309 (BBC News)]
